subject: sleep in slave pen
fact: Everyone’s sleep in the slave pen is troubled and fitful, filled with strange dreams and disturbing images. Dark shadows seem to move and reach out toward them as the characters wander lost through endless mazes of tunnels. Oily tentacles slide to brush up against them while a great buzzing and howling rises in the distance. Suppurating wounds burst open in clouds of spores or crawling masses of maggots or insects. At least one or more of the prisoners wakes in a cold sweat from these nightmares after every rest, feeling as though something is out there in the dark depths — something far worse than the drow.

fact: Deep gnomes are present as prisoners Topsy and Turvy, who steal knives during Gyrgum’s cooking.

subject: Deep gnomes
fact: Deep gnomes, represented by Topsy and Shuushar, are known for their knowledge of Underdark routes and their desire to share enlightenment. They advocate for Blingdenstone and Menzoberranzan as escape paths, respectively.
source_quote: Topsy says, “We should go to Blingdenstone. I know there is a way out of the Underdark from there.” Shuushar objects, “Yes, but the direct path is through Menzoberranzan. We will have to go to Darklake first, and we must visit my people to share the enlightenment! From there, the path is good.”

subject: derro
fact: Derro are present as prisoners, including Buppido, who believes he is divine and speaks of a divine plan.
source_quote: Buppido speaks, or instead projects his mind, “The Divine plan says we must collaborate and share information.” ... Daz learns from the cleric that Buppido thinks he is some kind of god, or he is a god.

subject: Derros
fact: Derros, represented by Jimjar, are twisted, greedy dwarves who thrive in chaos and often engage in betting and manipulation. Jimjar wagers on the newcomers’ choices.
source_quote: Jimjar adds, “Who wants to bet on which path the new guys will want to go? Will they go with the myconid kid? The enlightened kuo-toan? The Destiny Weilding Derro? Or trust the two deep gnomes?”

subject: drow
fact: Drow worship Lolth as their spider goddess and operate the outpost as a religious and military center.
source_quote: This place is a shrine to Lolth, the drow’s spider goddess.

subject: Drow
fact: The Drow are an organized group that hoards loot, assigns tasks, and is viewed by prisoners as exploitative and distrustful.
source_quote: The Drow leader probably keeps all the loot for herself. And if any other Drow had our stuff, they would taunt us.

subject: Drow Outpost
fact: The Drow Outpost is a floating facility 100’ in the sky, accessible only by winch and basket systems; it includes a mess hall with zurkhwood tables, a food storage area, and a cave used for gathering; it is staffed by Drow overseers, Quaggoth and Kuo-Toan prisoners, and maintains strict control over labor and punishment.
source_quote: The Drow outpost was 100’ in the sky. A direct drop would be suicidal.

subject: drow warriors
fact: Drow warriors gather in the mess hall cave, which serves as their eating and gathering place.
source_quote: The cave serves as a gathering and eating place for the drow warriors of the outpost.

subject: Ilvara’s polycule
fact: Ilvara’s polycule is a drow power structure that operates through shifting alliances and hierarchies, with members like Jorlan, Shoor, Sethir, and others rising and falling based on loyalty, utility, and physical condition. It controls the slave pen and the prisoners' fate.
source_quote: Sethir says, “That’s Jorlan. He used to be the number one, but after he got hit with acid, his face was disfigured and he lost a finger, Ilvara’s dropped him, and now Shoor is number one.”

subject: kuo-toa
fact: Kuo-toa are present as prisoners, including Shuushar the Awakened, who seeks spiritual balance.
source_quote: The Kuo-Toan Shuushar the Awakened notices and tells him to relax... Shuushar mutters, “I see.”

subject: Kuo-toans
fact: Kuo-toans, represented by Shuushar, are fish-like aberrations who believe in enlightenment and ritual. They insist on visiting their people before proceeding on escape routes.
source_quote: Shuushar objects, “Yes, but the direct path is through Menzoberranzan. We will have to go to Darklake first, and we must visit my people to share the enlightenment! From there, the path is good.”

subject: Lolth-worshippers
fact: Lolth-worshippers are drow who follow the Spider Queen and maintain a rigid, cruel hierarchy. There is no known abolitionist movement among them, and any aid offered to prisoners is assumed to serve their own interests.
source_quote: Prince Derendil explains, “Well we know that there is no abolitionist movement amongst those who worship Lolth. It has to be for his benefit.”

subject: myconid
fact: Myconids are referenced as a potential destination group, with Stool being their representative.
source_quote: Stool objects, “No to the great circle! My people!”

subject: Myconids
fact: The myconids are a fungal race with a communal culture, represented by Stool, who opposes routes that endanger their sacred circle and prioritize their people’s safety.
source_quote: Stool objects, “No to the great circle! My people!”

subject: The Drow of the Priestess’s Tower
fact: The drow of the priestess’s tower are a rigid, hierarchical society devoted to Lolth; they enforce slavery through terror, use spider symbolism in architecture and worship, and maintain control via ritualized violence, surveillance, and psychological domination; their priestess, Ilvara, wields absolute authority.
source_quote: This place is a shrine to Lolth, the drow’s spider goddess. The altar is flanked by a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each. They hold thick black candles and are unlit.

subject: The Prisoner Collective
fact: The prisoner collective is an ad hoc alliance of diverse races (dwarves, gnomes, orcs, derros, elves) bound by shared captivity; they communicate via spore-induced group minds, coordinated thefts, and shared planning; despite internal differences, they are beginning to unify under the influence of Buppido’s delusions and Thorin’s pragmatic leadership.
source_quote: Jimjar is making more bets. The stool is happy to be talking to everyone and has spread his spores so that everyone in the prison cell is in a group mind. ... Daz notes that this allows them to coordinate any plans without being discovered.

subject: armory
fact: The armory is the target location after the prison door is opened and a distraction is created, where weapons must be seized for escape.
source_quote: Jorlan smiles, “I will leave the door to the prison open, create a distraction. The path to the armory will be unguarded. Grab the weapons and flee.”

subject: Blingdenstone
fact: Blingdenstone is a deep gnome city with a known exit from the Underdark, advocated by Topsy as a safe escape route.
source_quote: Topsy says, “We should go to Blingdenstone. I know there is a way out of the Underdark from there.”

subject: bridge near the waterfall

source_quote: As he crosses the bridge near the waterfall... attached to the edge of the barracks platform is a winch-and-basket device consisting of a giant swinging arm that carries a thin cord of strong spider silk. The cord runs through several pulleys from a hand-cranked horizontal spool to a heavy woven basket suspended at the end.

subject: Gyrgum
fact: Gyrgum is an orc chef whose theatrical cooking has become legendary among the prisoners; his skill is so extraordinary that even Shuushar suggests his cooking might be mistaken for divine, and he is now being observed by drow soldiers who are entertained by his performances.
source_quote: Shuushar cautioned the orc, 'If you were to show this cooking to my people, they might imagine a god like you.'

subject: Gyrgum
fact: Gyrgum is assigned to cooking duties with Shuushar, Topsy, and Turvy.
source_quote: Then, at last, it’s Gyrgum’s turn. A Drow appears and points at Shuushar, Topsy, Turvy, and Gyrgum.

subject: Gyrgum
fact: Gyrgum is worried about being led by the Drow with Ront and Prince Derendil.

subject: Gyrgum
fact: Gyrgum thinks not speaking Undercommon is awkward but manageable because others can translate.
source_quote: Not speaking undercommon is awkward, but then again, understanding the language of your captors may be a problem. And anyway, I’ve got plenty of folks around me who can translate.

subject: Gyrgum

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a drow leader who maintains control over the group through her polycule hierarchy. She has discarded Jorlan and elevated Shoor, and is implied to hoard all loot, including the prisoners' belongings.
source_quote: Thorin thinks for a moment, “I know where our stuff is. It’s in the chest in Ilvara’s room. The Drow leader probably keeps all the loot for herself. And if any other Drow had our stuff, they would taunt us.”

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is the Drow leader who keeps loot in her room.
source_quote: It’s in the chest in Ilvara’s room. The Drow leader probably keeps all the loot for herself.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is the high priestess of Lolth and commander of the outpost, who uses a scourge and demands obedience.
source_quote: Ilvara is there. She smiles and has her scourge handy... “I am the high priestess of Lolth and commander. Do not spill any water, do not touch anything, and fill my bath.”

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is the high priestess of Lolth and commander of the priestess’s tower; she is cold, calculating, and terrifyingly precise in her control over slaves, wielding a scourge and enforcing obedience with threats of violence; her quarters are a shrine-like chamber adorned with dark silken mats, a zurkhwood pedestal, and a sculpted spider idol with jet eyes.
source_quote: Ilvara smiled and had her scourge handy as she flicked it toward her prisoners. 'This is my quarters. I am the high priestess of Lolth and commander. Do not spill any water, do not touch anything, and fill my bath.'

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara smiles and holds her scourge as she speaks to prisoners.
source_quote: Ilvara is there. She smiles and has her scourge handy as she flicks it toward her prisoners.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara uses a scourge to remind slaves to obey.
source_quote: Mistress Ilvara liked to impress her will with a scourge in hand and remind her slaves that our lives now belong to her.

subject: Ilvara

source_quote: Thorin recalls how Ilvara was in charge when they first arrived here.

subject: Ilvara

source_quote: As Thorin stares at Ilvara some more, he realizes there is something manic about her.

subject: Imbros
fact: Imbros is a Drow overseer who commands Gyrgum, Shuushar, Topsy, and Turvy to cook; his authority is recognized by the prisoners; he is referenced but not directly seen in the scene.
source_quote: Excellent, Imbros wants us to cook.

subject: Imbros

source_quote: Excellent, Imbros wants us to cook.

subject: Jaezred

source_quote: There are a pair of Drow sitting at a table, looking hungry. Shuushar mutters: “Jaezred and Kalannar”

subject: Jimjar

source_quote: Wanna bet on who would die first when we splat on the ground?

source_quote: Jimjar adds, “Who wants to bet on which path the new guys will want to go? Will they go with the myconid kid? The enlightened kuo-toan? The Destiny Weilding Derro? Or trust the two deep gnomes?”

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar is a prisoner who constantly tries to make bets about the dangers of the outpost; he speculates on who will die first when falling, how many buckets will be filled, and how many times the basket will be dropped; he is assigned to the winch crew with Zalthir and others; he mutters darkly about the risks and engages others in morbid wagers.
source_quote: Wanna bet on who would die first when we splat on the ground?

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar is a prisoner who repeatedly tries to make bets about the winch operations and escape routes.
source_quote: Jimjar, next to him, mutters, “Wanna bet on who would die first when we splat on the ground?” ... Jimjar again tries to make a bet... Jimjar adds, “Who wants to bet on which path the new guys will want to go?”

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a former leader of Ilvara’s polycule, disfigured by acid and discarded after losing a finger. He offers to help the prisoners escape to embarrass Shoor and make Ilvara regret her mistake. He opens the prison door, creates a distraction, and guides them toward the armory.
source_quote: Jorlan says, “That’s Jorlan. He used to be the number one, but after he got hit with acid, his face was disfigured and he lost a finger, Ilvara’s dropped him, and now Shoor is number one.” Jorlan turns to Thorin, “If I made it possible for you to escape, would you try?”

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a former number-one servant of Ilvara who was disfigured by acid and now offers to help the prisoners escape.
source_quote: Sethir says, “That’s Jorlan. He used to be the number one, but after he got hit with acid, his face was disfigured and he lost a finger, Ilvara’s dropped him... Jorlan turns to Thorin, “If I made it possible for you to escape, would you try?”

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan says, “I don’t care if you succeed. I just want you to try. It will make Shoor look ridiculous, and make Ilvara realize what a terrible mistake she’s made. And if you do make a mistake, she’ll be embarrassed and need my help to find you and realize what a mistake she made.”

subject: Jorlan

source_quote: Prince Derendil mutters, “ I remember how she greeted me when I arrived. She was robed in silken garments and flanked by two male drow, one of whom had a mass of scars along one side of his face and neck. Mistress Ilvara liked to impress her will with a scourge in hand and remind her slaves that our lives now belong to her. Every time, she would end her pep talks with the phrase - ‘Accept your fate, learn to obey, and you may survive.’”

subject: Prince Derendil

subject: Sethir

source_quote: Sethir says, “That’s Jorlan. He used to be the number one, but after he got hit with acid, his face was disfigured and he lost a finger, Ilvara’s dropped him, and now Shoor is number one.” Daz wakes up and remembers, “Right, Sethir said there is a grey ooze in the pool. That’s how the waste gets processed.”

subject: Sethir

source_quote: Sethir says, “... now Shoor is number one.”

subject: Shuushar
fact: Shuushar has chosen not to repeat offensive words as part of his spiritual balance.
source_quote: As part of my attempt to find spiritual balance and cope with the madness of my race, I have chosen not to repeat offensive words.

subject: Shuushar
fact: Shuushar is a Kuo-Toan who translates Drow speech for Gyrgum and cautions him about cooking being a better distraction.
source_quote: The Kuo-Toan Shuushar the Awakened notices and tells him to relax... Shuushar translates, “Can you cook? That would be a better distraction.”

subject: Shuushar

source_quote: I have chosen not to repeat offensive words.

subject: Thorin

subject: Thorin

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf who recalls chaotic conversations from his youth, and is surprised when a member of Ilvara’s polycule brings food. He connects to his companions via spores to question Jorlan’s motives, and ultimately accepts the escape plan after Jorlan’s assurances.
source_quote: Thorin connected to his friends via the spores and asked, “How do we know that he isn’t here to entrap us?” Thorin is satisfied. “What’s the plan?”

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir considers fire-breathing as a simpler way to cut the rope.
source_quote: But I breathe fire, and fire breathing is a simpler way to cut a rope…

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a dragonborn monk detailed to the winch, tasked with cleaning up after Daz, Stool, and Sarith, and now uses the cleaning to examine how to damage the winch to aid escape. He is focused on spider silk's role in the mechanism and considers fire-breathing as a means to cut ropes. He took a piece of rope to test its resistance later.
source_quote: But I breathe fire, and fire breathing is a simpler way to cut a rope… He takes a small piece of rope to test its resistance later.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a dragonborn monk who notices a spider web, a pool of water, and pockets a piece of paper.
source_quote: Zalthir notices a spider web. Below the spider’s web, he notices a pool of water. ... He pockets the paper.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a prisoner who notices environmental details such as spider webs, water pools, and a paper with names of debtors; he pockets the paper after noticing it in the basket; he observes Elspeth taking a comb and realizes he has little use for it; he is assigned to clean and unload cargo with Balok's group; he is aware of the lethal drop from the outpost and the danger of the winch system.
source_quote: It’s unclear where, which city, what favor, and why.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is assigned to the winch again on the next day.
source_quote: The dragonborn monk is once again detailed to the winch.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is pointed out by a Drow for cargo-loading duties.
source_quote: The next Drow appears and points to Zalthir, Buppido, Jimjar, and Eldeth.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observes that the speaker seems confident they will escape and live.
source_quote: Zalthir says, “You seem to be confident we will escape and live.”

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir says, 'You seem to be confident we will escape and live.'
source_quote: Zalthir says, "You seem to be confident we will escape and live."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir walks by while Thorin fills his bucket.
source_quote: As he fills his bucket, he notices Zalthir walking by.

subject: black candles
fact: The silver candlesticks hold thick black candles and are unlit.
source_quote: They hold thick black candles and are unlit.

subject: black-stained zurkhwood chest
fact: A heavy chest of black-stained zurkhwood sits at the foot of Ilvara’s bed.
source_quote: A heavy chest of black-stained zurkhwood sits at the foot of the bed.

subject: chest
fact: The chest holds the prisoners’ belongings and is located in Ilvara’s room.
source_quote: It’s in the chest in Ilvara’s room.

subject: chest
fact: The chest is located in Ilvara’s room and contains the prisoners’ belongings.
source_quote: It’s in the chest in Ilvara’s room.

subject: chest in Ilvara’s room
fact: The chest in Ilvara’s room contains the prisoners' personal belongings, which Thorin identifies as the key to reclaiming their gear before escape.
source_quote: Thorin thinks for a moment, “I know where our stuff is. It’s in the chest in Ilvara’s room. The Drow leader probably keeps all the loot for herself. And if any other Drow had our stuff, they would taunt us.”

subject: Comb
fact: A comb is found and pocketed by Elspeth after Zalthir takes the paper; it has no apparent utility to the prisoners; its origin and purpose are unclear.
source_quote: She pockets the comb. He has little use for combs.

subject: comb
fact: Eldeth finds and pockets a comb.
source_quote: He notices that Elspeth sees him pocket the paper. He notices that she finds a comb. She pockets the comb.

subject: comb
fact: Elspeth finds and pockets a comb while Zalthir pockets the piece of paper.
source_quote: He notices that Elspeth sees him pocket the paper. He notices that she finds a comb. She pockets the comb.

source_quote: and the winch and gears that the spider silk goes through.

source_quote: a hand-cranked horizontal spool

source_quote: A heavy iron brazier provides cooking heat and dim light

subject: heavy woven basket
fact: The winch-and-basket device suspends a heavy woven basket.
source_quote: a heavy woven basket suspended at the end.

subject: Ilvara’s Scourge
fact: Ilvara’s Scourge is a whip-like instrument of control, always kept handy; it is used to flick warnings at prisoners and enforce obedience; its presence is a constant psychological threat, symbolizing the drow’s mastery over pain and submission.
source_quote: Ilvara is there. She smiles and has her scourge handy as she flicks it toward her prisoners.

subject: iron brazier
fact: A heavy iron brazier provides cooking heat and dim light in the mess hall.
source_quote: A heavy iron brazier provides cooking heat and dim light

subject: jet eyes of spider statue
fact: The eight eyes of the spider statue are polished jet: four small ones worth 5 gp each and four larger ones worth 10 gp each.
source_quote: The eight “eyes” of the spider statue are eight pieces of polished jet — four small ones worth five gp each and four larger ones worth ten gp each.

subject: Knife
fact: A knife is present in the kitchen area; Gyrgum attempts to steal it to sharpen it; Guldor takes it and delivers a clear threat of punishment; it is a tool of utility and potential rebellion.
source_quote: They will do awful things to you if you steal a knife.

subject: knife
fact: Gyrgum attempts to steal a knife from the kitchen, and Topsy and Turvy later steal several knives.
source_quote: Grygum notices a knife and tries to steal it. ... Topsy and Turvy steal several knives.

subject: knife
fact: Gyrgum tries to steal a knife from the kitchen.
source_quote: As the lunch progresses, Grygum notices a knife and tries to steal it.

subject: large jet eyes value
fact: The four larger jet eyes of the spider statue are worth ten gp each.
source_quote: four larger ones worth ten gp each

subject: Paper with Names of Debtors
fact: A piece of paper found in the basket lists names of individuals who owe favors to its holder; the location, nature of the favors, and reason for the list are unknown; Zalthir pockets it despite not understanding its full context.
source_quote: A piece of paper with some names of people who owe a favor to the person who has the paper.

subject: piece of paper
fact: Zalthir finds a piece of paper with names of people who owe a favor, and pockets it.
source_quote: As the basket bounces, Zalthir notices a piece of paper with some names of people who owe a favor to the person who has the paper.

subject: piece of rope

source_quote: A rope ladder leads down from the shrine into this chamber.

source_quote: The altar is flanked by a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each.

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The pair of heavy silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: small jet eyes value
fact: The four small jet eyes of the spider statue are worth five gp each.
source_quote: four small ones worth five gp each

subject: spider silk
fact: Spider silk is used in the winch mechanism, passing through the gears and basket. Zalthir examines it as a potential point of sabotage.
source_quote: The two things that attract his attention are using spider silk to hold the basket and the winch and gears that the spider silk goes through.

subject: spider silk
fact: Zalthir notices the spider silk holds the basket and winch.
source_quote: The two things that attract his attention are using spider silk to hold the basket and the winch

subject: spider silk cord
fact: The winch-and-basket device uses a thin cord of strong spider silk.
source_quote: a thin cord of strong spider silk

subject: The Silver Candlesticks
fact: Two heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each flank the altar of Lolth; they hold thick black candles that remain unlit, suggesting ritual neglect, symbolic absence of divine light, or a waiting for a future moment of revelation.
source_quote: The altar is flanked by a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each. They hold thick black candles and are unlit.

subject: The Spider Idol of Lolth
fact: The Spider Idol is a 10-foot-tall sculpture carved from zurkhwood, placed atop a pedestal at the center of the Priestess’s Tower; its eight eyes are made of polished jet, four small (5 gp each) and four large (10 gp each); it is the focal point of worship and symbolizes Lolth’s dominion over the drow.
source_quote: In the middle of the chamber (at the center of the web) stands a broad pedestal carved from zurkhwood, with a 10-foot-high sculpted spider at its head.

subject: Basket Drop Ritual
fact: The ritualistic dropping of the basket by the Quahogs, accompanied by laughter from Balok and expected reactions from prisoners, suggests a pattern of psychological torture or control; its frequency and purpose are unexplained.
source_quote: The two quahogs let it drop. The other prisoners are startled but seem to have been expecting this. Balok is laughing.

subject: Buppido's divine plan
fact: Buppido claims a divine plan requires escape and distraction, but the nature of the plan is vague and unverified.
source_quote: The divine plan requires that you create a distraction while I escape.

subject: Buppido’s True Nature
fact: Buppido claims to be a god or divine entity, but his insanity is recognized by Thorin and others; whether he is delusional, possessed, or genuinely divine remains unresolved — his influence grows even as his credibility falters.
source_quote: Daz learns from the cleric that Buppido thinks he is some kind of god, or he is a god.

subject: debt repayment system
fact: A system of wagers and future collection has been established for debts, with no money currently available. The group must survive and earn money to settle obligations.
source_quote: Zalthir asks, “We have no money; how do we pay our debts?” “Oh, don’t worry, I have perfect recall. Just make your wager, and when you have money, I’ll collect.”

subject: divine plan
fact: Buppido claims a divine plan requires collaboration, information sharing, and distraction for his escape.
source_quote: Buppido speaks, or instead projects his mind, “The Divine plan says we must collaborate and share information.” ... Buppido says, “The divine plan requires that you create a distraction while I escape.”

subject: escape planning
fact: The prisoners are discussing multiple escape routes: Gracklstugh, Blingdenstone, Darklake, and using waterfall or spiderwebs.
source_quote: Buppido smiles, “To Gracklstugh, my homeland!” ... Topsy says, “We should go to Blingdenstone. I know there is a way out of the Underdark from there.” ... Shuushar objects, “Yes, but the direct path is through Menzoberranzan. We will have to go to Darklake first...” ... Jorlan says, “Use the waterfall to slide down, or jump into the spiderwebs and then jump into the pools of water.”

subject: escape plan sequence
fact: The escape plan involves Jorlan leaving the prison door open, then reaching the armory, then using the waterfall or spiderwebs, then choosing a destination.
source_quote: I will leave the door to the prison open, create a distraction. The path to the armory will be unguarded. Grab the weapons and flee. Use the waterfall to slide down, or jump into the spiderwebs and then jump into the pools of water. To Gracklstugh... to Blingdenstone... go to Darklake first...

subject: escape route decision
fact: The group is divided on the optimal escape route, with competing proposals from myconids, deep gnomes, kuo-toans, and others. The decision remains unresolved and is the subject of betting and suspicion.
source_quote: Jimjar adds, “Who wants to bet on which path the new guys will want to go? Will they go with the myconid kid? The enlightened kuo-toan? The Destiny Weilding Derro? Or trust the two deep gnomes?”

subject: group mind
fact: Stool’s spores create a group mind among the prisoners, enabling covert coordination.
source_quote: The stool is happy to be talking to everyone and has spread his spores so that everyone in the prison cell is in a group mind. ... Daz notes that this allows them to coordinate any plans without being discovered.

subject: Ilvara’s pep talk
fact: Prince Derendil recalls Ilvara’s phrase: ‘Accept your fate, learn to obey, and you may survive.’
source_quote: Mistress Ilvara liked to impress her will with a scourge in hand and remind her slaves that our lives now belong to her. Every time, she would end her pep talks with the phrase - ‘Accept your fate, learn to obey, and you may survive.’

subject: Jorlan's true motives
fact: Jorlan offers to help the prisoners escape, but his motives are unclear and unverified.
source_quote: I don’t care if you succeed. I just want you to try. It will make Shoor look ridiculous, and make Ilvara realize what a terrible mistake she’s made.

subject: nightmares in the slave pen
fact: All prisoners suffer from recurring, vivid nightmares filled with moving shadows, oily tentacles, buzzing, howling, and erupting wounds. At least one wakes in cold sweat after every rest, sensing something far worse than the drow.
source_quote: Everyone’s sleep in the slave pen is troubled and fitful, filled with strange dreams and disturbing images. Dark shadows seem to move and reach out toward them as the characters wander lost through endless mazes of tunnels. Oily tentacles slide to brush up against them while a great buzzing and howling rises in the distance. Suppurating wounds burst open in clouds of spores or crawling masses of maggots or insects. At least one or more of the prisoners wakes in a cold sweat from these nightmares after every rest, feeling as though something is out there in the dark depths — something far worse than the drow.

subject: Paper of Debtors
fact: The paper with names of debtors is an unresolved plot thread; its origin, the identity of the holder, the nature of the favors owed, and the location of the debts are unknown; Zalthir has pocketed it, suggesting future relevance.
source_quote: It’s unclear where, which city, what favor, and why.

subject: something far worse than the drow
fact: Prisoners feel something far worse than the Drow is present in the dark depths, emerging from their nightmares.
source_quote: something far worse than the drow

subject: Spiritual Balance of Shuushar
fact: Shuushar's claim of spiritual balance through avoiding offensive language is a recurring thread; his selective translation and moral posturing suggest deeper psychological conflict and potential betrayal or manipulation.
source_quote: As part of my attempt to find spiritual balance and cope with the madness of my race, I have chosen not to repeat offensive words.

subject: Stool's home
fact: Stool wants to return to his people, but the location of his home is not specified in this session.
source_quote: Stool objects, “No to the great circle! My people!”

subject: The Clean Lake Mystery
fact: Despite daily deposits of filth from the tower’s chamber pots, the lake remains unnaturally clean with no visible source of purification; this suggests magical intervention, hidden drainage, or a deeper secret controlled by the drow.
source_quote: They look around and see nothing.

subject: The Scourge and the Spider
fact: The recurring imagery of the scourge and the spider idol suggests a deeper ritual or prophecy tied to Lolth’s worship; the unlit candles and the spider’s jet eyes may be components of a pending sacrifice or awakening.
source_quote: Ilvara liked to impress her will with a scourge in hand... This place is a shrine to Lolth, the drow’s spider goddess.

subject: trust in Jorlan
fact: The prisoners are uncertain whether Jorlan’s aid is genuine or a trap set by Ilvara. Thorin voices suspicion, and Jorlan acknowledges their distrust, deepening the mystery.
source_quote: Thorin connected to his friends via the spores and asked, “How do we know that he isn’t here to entrap us?” Jorlan smiles, “I can sense you don’t trust me. You are wise not to trust me.”

subject: wager
fact: A wager is made about escaping and living, to be collected after a long rest.
source_quote: “Wanna bet?”

subject: wager
fact: The wager will be collected after a long rest, before assigned tasks.
source_quote: “After a long rest, before you go on your assigned tasks.”

subject: Zalthir's escape plan
fact: Zalthir considers using fire to cut the spider silk or ice to break gears, but no decision is made.
source_quote: But I breathe fire, and fire breathing is a simpler way to cut a rope…
